topics.title: Boat engines & spawning
topics.takeaway: Manual driver exit now stops the engine automatically. Driver death keeps it running and still prevents transport-boat spawning.
topics.caution: This engine rule is separate from missing-spawn and asset-replication reports; the linked bug record retains the latest investigation and fix status.

changes.summary: Manual driver exit now stops the engine automatically. Driver death keeps the engine running and can still deny spawning.
changes.before: Leaving the driver seat did not automatically stop the engine.
changes.after: Manual exit switches the engine off. Driver death in the seat leaves it running.

topics.overview: Leaving a transport boat’s driver seat now switches its engine off. Being killed in the seat leaves it running.
topics.context: Transport-boat spawning requires the engine to be off. The update distinguishes a driver leaving the seat from a driver being killed there.

baselines.title: Transport boat engine shutdown
baselines.summary: Manual driver exit switches the engine off. Driver death in the seat leaves it running, which prevents transport-boat spawning until it is switched off.

issues.title: Spawn choices and Commander abilities can disappear
issues.bottom_line: Developers have another spawn/asset replication fix prepared for the next update. Earlier changes reduced reports, but the additional fix is not confirmed released and remaining cases stay open.

topics.title: Fortification costs & limits
topics.takeaway: Level 1 defenses cost no Supplies; upgrades still do. Barbed Wire increased from two to three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.
topics.caution: Free Level 1 construction does not remove upgrade costs or placement limits. Announced future defensive additions are outside these released rules.

changes.summary: Level 1 construction stopped consuming Supplies; higher-level upgrades still require them.
changes.before: Basic Level 1 construction consumed Supplies.
changes.after: Level 1 construction costs no Supplies. Higher-level upgrades still require Supplies.

changes.summary: Barbed Wire increased from two to three placements per Engineer, with a limit of 50 per side.
changes.before: Two Barbed Wire placements per Engineer.
changes.after: Three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.

topics.overview: Basic defenses no longer require Supplies to build. Engineers can also place more Barbed Wire.
topics.context: These changes affect the Supplies needed for Engineer-built defenses and the number of Barbed Wire placements allowed.

baselines.title: Engineer buildables & Barbed Wire
baselines.summary: Level 1 construction remains free of Supplies; upgrades still cost Supplies. Barbed Wire is now three per Engineer, capped at 50 per side.

topics.title: Redeploy timer change
topics.takeaway: The additional ten-second Redeploy punishment was removed; the normal deployment wait remains.
topics.caution: This change does not mean instant spawning or guarantee that a spawn point is available.

changes.summary: Removed the additional ten-second punishment for choosing Redeploy.
changes.before: Choosing Redeploy added a ten-second punishment.
changes.after: That extra punishment is removed. The normal deployment timer still applies.

topics.overview: Choosing Redeploy no longer adds an extra ten-second wait. The normal deployment timer still applies.
topics.context: The removed punishment was additional to the normal deployment timer.

baselines.title: Redeploy punishment timer
baselines.summary: Choosing Redeploy no longer adds a ten-second punishment; the normal deployment timer still applies.

topics.title: Tank ammunition changes
topics.takeaway: Selecting another shell type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the chosen ammunition.
topics.caution: The notes establish unloading and reloading, not an instant ammunition swap.

changes.summary: Added shell unloading when changing ammunition types.
changes.before: The loaded round had to be fired before changing shell types.
changes.after: Changing type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the selected type.

topics.overview: Tanks can now change their loaded ammunition type without firing the round already in the gun.
topics.context: The change concerns a round already loaded in the tank’s gun when a different ammunition type is selected.

baselines.title: Tank shell unloading
baselines.summary: Selecting another shell type unloads the chambered round and automatically loads the chosen type.

issues.title: Tank gunner seat changes silently switch ammunition to AP
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 fixes leaving or changing the Gunner seat switching ammunition to AP while the display still shows the previous shell.

topics.title: Medic & Rifleman slots
topics.takeaway: Medic slots increased from one to two per unit; Rifleman slots decreased from three to two.
topics.caution: Further Medic proposals are excluded from this released slot change.

changes.summary: Added a second Medic slot and reduced Rifleman slots from three to two.
changes.before: One Medic slot and three Rifleman slots per unit.
changes.after: Two Medic slots and two Rifleman slots per unit.

topics.overview: Each unit now has room for two Medics and two Riflemen, instead of one Medic and three Riflemen.
topics.context: The change reallocates the number of players who can hold each of these roles in a unit.

baselines.title: Unit composition & Medics
baselines.summary: Units have two Medic slots and two Rifleman slots, replacing one and three respectively.

topics.title: New US weapons & magazines
topics.takeaway: Selected US roles gained the M1A1 Thompson. The M16A1 now offers 30-round magazines alongside the 20-round option, with increased Weight costs.
topics.caution: Thompson access is role-specific. Exact role access and magazine Weight values are included in the current rules below.

changes.summary: Added the M1A1 Thompson to selected US roles and an optional 30-round M16A1 configuration.
changes.before: The listed US roles did not have the Thompson option. The existing M16A1 magazine option held 20 rounds.
changes.after: The Thompson is available to the listed US roles. M16A1 users can select 30-round magazines; the 20-round option remains.

topics.overview: Some US roles gained the Thompson submachine gun. The M16A1 gained an optional larger magazine.
topics.context: These are US loadout additions. The 20-round M16A1 configuration remains available.

baselines.title: M1A1 Thompson
baselines.summary: US access: Commander, Tank Commander, Crewman, Mortar Observer, Sniper, Squad Leader, Medic, Specialist, Grenadier and Engineer.

baselines.title: M16A1 30-round magazines
baselines.summary: Optional 30-round configuration: six magazines by default, up to ten via Barracks. The weapon gains one Weight; each magazine costs two Weight versus one for a 20-round magazine.

topics.title: Boat handling & Fuel costs
topics.takeaway: Both boats gained handling and top-speed improvements. The US PBR’s speed advantage increased; the NVA boat rose from 200 to 250 Fuel.
topics.caution: The notes describe relative handling and speed changes; exact speed and acceleration values are not supplied.

changes.summary: Improved both boats’ handling and top speed, increased the US PBR’s relative speed and acceleration advantage, and raised the NVA boat’s Fuel cost by 50.
changes.before: The NVA boat cost 200 Fuel. Earlier speed and handling values are not quantified in these notes.
changes.after: The NVA boat costs 250 Fuel. Both boats have improved handling and top speed, with a larger US PBR speed and acceleration advantage.

topics.overview: Both factions’ boats received handling and speed changes. The NVA boat also costs more Fuel.
topics.context: The release changes boat movement and the Fuel cost of the supply-carrying NVA boat.

baselines.title: Boat handling, speed & Fuel balance
baselines.summary: Both factions gain handling and top-speed improvements. The US PBR has a larger speed/acceleration advantage; the supply-carrying NVA boat now costs 250 Fuel, up from 200.

topics.title: Vehicle machine-gun resupply
topics.takeaway: Tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions can now be resupplied before their ammunition runs out.
topics.caution: Equal resupply of the two boat bow guns is a separate reported issue and is not explicitly confirmed fixed by this change.

changes.summary: Allowed ammunition top-ups before empty for tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions.
changes.before: These guns had to be completely empty before receiving more ammunition.
changes.after: They can receive ammunition while some rounds remain.

topics.overview: Some tank and boat machine guns can now receive more ammunition before they are completely empty.
topics.context: The update applies to tank coaxial machine guns and boat Machine Gunner positions.

baselines.title: Tank coaxial & boat MG ammunition top-ups
baselines.summary: Tank coaxial MGs and boat Machine Gunner positions can be resupplied before their ammunition is completely empty.

issues.title: Dual bow boat guns may reload only one weapon
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 permits boat-gun top-ups before empty. The separate report that only one dual bow gun reloads is not explicitly confirmed fixed.

topics.title: Controller Crouch / Melee swap
topics.takeaway: All controller layouts now offer a Crouch / Melee input swap.
topics.caution: This released option only swaps Crouch and Melee. Other controller options and Tactical Map changes retain their own development status in the content tracker.

changes.summary: Released the Crouch / Melee input swap for controller layouts.
changes.before: The Crouch / Melee swap was a planned addition.
changes.after: The swap is available across all controller layouts.

topics.overview: Controller users gained an option to swap the Crouch and Melee inputs.
topics.context: This adds a specific two-input swap to the existing controller layouts.

baselines.title: Controller Crouch / Melee swap
baselines.summary: All controller layouts offer a Crouch / Melee input swap.

topics.title: Commander ability penalties
topics.takeaway: Team-kill punishment was removed for Commander abilities; personal weapons and other direct actions retain their usual punishment behavior.
topics.caution: This changes punishment for Commander abilities. It does not remove friendly fire or all penalties.

changes.summary: Removed Commander team-kill punishment for friendly deaths caused by abilities such as Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs.
changes.before: Friendly deaths from Commander abilities could add a team-kill punishment to the Commander.
changes.after: Those ability-related deaths no longer add that punishment. Personal weapons and other direct actions retain their usual punishment behavior.

topics.overview: Friendly deaths caused by Commander abilities no longer add the associated punishment to the Commander.
topics.context: The affected abilities include Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs.

baselines.title: Commander ability team-kill punishment
baselines.summary: Friendly deaths from Commander abilities such as Napalm, Artillery Strikes and Bombing Runs no longer add a team-kill punishment to the Commander.

topics.title: Graphics & display options
topics.overview: PS5 Pro, compatible PS5 displays and supported AMD PC graphics cards gained different graphics options.
topics.takeaway: PS5 Pro gained PSSR; PS5 and PS5 Pro gained VRR on compatible displays. Supported AMD GPUs gained FSR Frame Generation.
topics.context: PSSR reconstructs the image on PS5 Pro. VRR matches display refresh to changing frame delivery. Frame Generation inserts extra frames on supported AMD hardware; these are separate technologies.
topics.caution: PSSR is specific to PS5 Pro, and VRR requires a compatible display. The AMD addition does not establish a fix for NVIDIA DLSS settings reports.

changes.summary: Released PSSR for PS5 Pro, VRR for compatible PS5 displays, and AMD FSR Frame Generation on supported 5000-series-and-newer GPUs.
changes.before: These PS5 and AMD options had not been released in the reviewed patch history. Xbox Series X|S already supported VRR.
changes.after: The new options are available on their supported hardware. They do not apply equally to every console or PC.

baselines.title: PS5 display options
baselines.summary: PSSR is available on PS5 Pro. VRR is available on PS5 and PS5 Pro with compatible displays.

baselines.title: AMD FSR Frame Generation
baselines.summary: Available in Video Settings on supported AMD GPUs, specified as 5000 series and newer. The publisher recommends a base rate around 60 FPS or higher to limit added latency.

issues.title: Console image quality
issues.bottom_line: PS5 Pro PSSR and compatible-display PS5 VRR are live from 1.7. Further visual work targets 2.0; base-PS5 QSSR still depends on Sony availability and is not confirmed released.

issues.title: Blurry foliage and disappearing cover
issues.bottom_line: Specific foliage and LOD corrections shipped in 1.7. The November 6 update confirms further visual-quality, performance and environmental-readability work for 2.0; broad resolution remains unverified.

issues.title: DLSS Frame Generation needs reapplying
issues.status_label: Fix in development · no release date
issues.bottom_line: Developers explicitly acknowledge NVIDIA Frame Generation needing reactivation after launch. A fix is in progress for an update in 2026, with no committed date or verified release.

topics.title: Finding & saving servers
topics.overview: The server list prioritises fuller matches. Filters and saved favourites received persistence fixes.
topics.takeaway: Higher-population servers move up the list. Filters survive a game restart, and Favourites saving and server targeting have release-documented fixes.
topics.context: These changes affect the order of the server list and whether choices survive between sessions. They are separate from the number of servers a player may save.
topics.caution: The released corrections do not establish that every missing-server report is resolved or that Favourites capacity has increased.

changes.summary: Prioritised fuller servers and corrected filter persistence and Favourites saving/targeting.
changes.before: Filters could reset after restarting, and Favourites could fail to save or select the intended server. Fuller-server ordering was not prioritised as it is now.
changes.after: Fuller servers are prioritised, selected filters persist, and the notes document corrections to Favourites saving and targeting.

baselines.title: Server Browser sorting & filters
baselines.summary: Fuller servers are prioritised; filters persist between sessions and Favourites target the correct server.

issues.title: Server Browser filters fail to persist
issues.bottom_line: The publisher reaffirmed on October 15 that filters persist. Independent outcome testing remains unrecorded.

issues.title: Servers missing from browser results
issues.bottom_line: Fuller-server ordering is reaffirmed; complete server discovery and removal of the earlier search limit remain unconfirmed.

issues.title: Favourite servers failed to save or targeted the wrong server
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.6: Corrects favourite persistence and server targeting. Independent outcome testing is not recorded.

topics.title: Vote Kick visibility & timing
topics.overview: Votes to remove a player are visible by default, with more time to respond.
topics.takeaway: Vote Kick notifications default to visible. The released changelog increases the response window from 15 to 30 seconds.
topics.context: Vote Kick lets players respond to a removal vote within their server. This update changes the notification default and the time available for a response.
topics.caution: Players can still choose to hide notifications. A longer, more visible vote does not establish that disruptive behavior has been eliminated.

changes.summary: Made Vote Kick notifications visible by default and doubled the voting window.
changes.before: The released changelog identifies a 15-second voting window and a default setting that hid Vote Kick notices.
changes.after: Votes allow 30 seconds, with notifications visible unless the player chooses to hide them.

baselines.title: Vote Kick visibility & voting time
baselines.summary: Vote Kick notifications default to visible; the response window increased from 15 to 30 seconds.

issues.title: Vote Kick visibility and response time
issues.bottom_line: The 1.6 visibility and 30-second response changes remain release-documented. The October 9 follow-up discusses positive feedback, not a new patch or proof trolling is solved.

topics.title: Official Server inactivity timer
topics.overview: Official Servers now remove inactive players after ten minutes instead of thirty.
topics.takeaway: The Official Server AFK timeout fell from 30 minutes to 10 minutes.
topics.context: AFK means inactive or away from the controls. This timer governs removal for inactivity while occupying a server slot.
topics.caution: The announcement specifies Official Servers. It does not establish a universal setting for community-run servers.

changes.summary: Reduced the Official Server inactivity timeout by twenty minutes.
changes.before: Official Servers used a 30-minute AFK timeout.
changes.after: Official Servers use a 10-minute AFK timeout.

baselines.title: Official Server AFK timer
baselines.summary: Official Servers now remove inactive players after ten minutes instead of thirty.

topics.title: Menus, settings & tutorial labels
topics.overview: Barracks menus have shorter transitions, unsaved settings trigger a warning, and tutorial completion labels are clearer.
topics.takeaway: Long Barracks camera transitions are removed. Leaving front-end Options with unsaved edits produces a prompt, and tutorial status labels distinguish completed from incomplete entries more clearly.
topics.context: These are menu and information-display changes. A clearer label and an unsaved-edit warning describe what the interface shows.
topics.caution: Neither change confirms that tutorial completion or every video setting will remain saved after restarting. Those reports retain separate bug records.

changes.summary: Shortened Barracks navigation and improved feedback about unsaved settings and tutorial completion.
changes.before: Barracks entry and exit used lengthy camera transitions. The new unsaved-edit prompt was absent, and tutorial completion labels were less clear.
changes.after: Barracks transitions are shorter, front-end Options warn about unsaved edits, and tutorial status is more clearly labelled.

baselines.title: Faster Barracks navigation & unsaved-options warning
baselines.summary: Lengthy Barracks entry/exit camera transitions are removed. Leaving front-end Options with unsaved edits now prompts the player.

baselines.title: Tutorial completion labels
baselines.summary: Tutorial status more clearly identifies completed and incomplete tutorials.

issues.title: Tutorial completion may not stay saved
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 clarifies tutorial completion labels. Saving lost completion progress is still not confirmed fixed.

issues.title: Video settings reported not saving after restart
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 adds an unsaved-options warning. That does not establish a fix for video settings failing to persist after restart.

topics.title: Unit naming
topics.overview: Units now use names such as Alfa, Bravo and Charlie from the NATO phonetic alphabet.
topics.takeaway: The Unit naming scheme changed to the NATO phonetic alphabet, including Alfa, Bravo and Charlie.
topics.context: These words identify lettered Units. Returning players may encounter a different spoken or displayed Unit name.
topics.caution: This change concerns Unit naming. It does not release Clan Tags or change the number of players in a Unit.

changes.summary: Changed the Unit naming scheme to NATO phonetic names.
changes.before: The previous naming scheme was replaced; this announcement does not enumerate every former name.
changes.after: Units use NATO phonetic names, including Alfa, Bravo, Charlie and Delta.

baselines.title: NATO phonetic Unit names
baselines.summary: Units use NATO phonetic names, including Alfa, Bravo and Charlie.

topics.title: Slow-vehicle collision deaths
topics.overview: Vehicles must be moving faster than before for an impact to kill infantry.
topics.takeaway: The vehicle speed required for a collision to kill infantry was raised again. The patch does not give the old or new speed threshold.
topics.context: This changes when a vehicle impact is lethal. It is separate from weapon damage to vehicles or vehicle movement speed.
topics.caution: No exact safe speed or immunity to vehicle impacts is established by the notes.

changes.summary: Raised the vehicle impact speed threshold again to reduce deaths from slowly moving vehicles.
changes.before: A lower vehicle speed could trigger a lethal infantry impact; no numerical threshold is provided.
changes.after: A higher speed is required for a lethal impact. The new threshold is not quantified.

baselines.title: Vehicle impact kill threshold
baselines.summary: Vehicles must reach a higher speed before an impact kills infantry; the notes give no numerical threshold.

topics.title: Commander limits & ability indicators
topics.overview: The Commander interface shows vehicle limits and whether the Encourage ability is active.
topics.takeaway: Vehicle Orders display the active vehicle limit. Patch 1.7 also documents an active-state indicator for Encourage.
topics.context: The display helps explain a vehicle-order limit and an ability’s current state. The notes describe interface feedback, not an increase to vehicle capacity.
topics.caution: Patch 1.6 already documented the vehicle-limit display and separately named a Reinforce indicator. The 1.7 notes name Encourage; they do not establish that the two ability names are interchangeable.

changes.summary: Documented vehicle-order active-limit information in the Commander interface.
changes.before: The vehicle-order limit was not shown through the added UI information.
changes.after: Vehicle Orders display how many vehicles of each type can be active.

changes.summary: Reiterated vehicle-limit information and documented an indicator for active Encourage.
changes.before: Vehicle-limit information was already documented in 1.6. That earlier changelog named a Reinforce indicator, not Encourage.
changes.after: The 1.7 notes explicitly describe active Encourage feedback alongside the vehicle-limit display.

baselines.title: Commander vehicle-limit & Encourage indicators
baselines.summary: Commander vehicle Orders show the active vehicle limit; Encourage has an active-state indicator.

issues.title: Simultaneous inputs prevent Commander vehicle orders
issues.bottom_line: Patch 1.7 fixes vehicle orders failing when multiple inputs are pressed together; this is not general spawn replication closure.

topics.title: Tunnel collapse during travel
topics.overview: A player travelling through a Tunnel dies immediately if that network collapses.
topics.takeaway: Tunnel-network collapse kills players in transit immediately, rather than waiting until their travel finishes. This was documented in 1.6 and restated in 1.7.
topics.context: This is the outcome when a network collapses while a player is travelling through it. It does not describe an ordinary completed Tunnel journey.
topics.caution: The rule does not establish a fix for every Tunnel connection, visibility or spawn-replication issue.

changes.summary: Moved the in-transit death to the moment the Tunnel network collapses.
changes.before: Death following a network collapse occurred when the Tunnel journey completed.
changes.after: A player in transit dies immediately when the network collapses; 1.7 later repeats this rule.

baselines.title: Tunnel-collapse travel outcome
baselines.summary: Players in transit are killed immediately if their Tunnel network collapses.

issues.title: Spawn choices and Commander abilities can disappear
issues.bottom_line: Developers have another spawn/asset replication fix prepared for the next update. Earlier changes reduced reports, but the additional fix is not confirmed released and remaining cases stay open.
